cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet living among the exiles in Babylon, tells this one himself (Ezekiel 1:1-3). Back at the start, God had him act out Jerusalem under siege as a sign to Israel (Ezekiel 4:1-3). Now, in the twelfth year of exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a man who escaped from Jerusalem finds him.

cards.question: What news does the man who escaped from Jerusalem bring Ezekiel?

cards.text: Here's the timing. Ezekiel has been mute, speaking only when God gives him a message (Ezekiel 3:26-27), but the evening before the man arrives, the hand of the LORD is on him.

cards.question: Before the man who escaped from Jerusalem shows up in the morning, the LORD opens Ezekiel's ___.

cards.text: Mouth open, back in business! Then the word of the LORD comes: back in Israel, the people living in the ruins are talking about one man from long ago who possessed the land.

cards.question: The people living in the ruins say ___ was only one man, yet he possessed the land.
Abraham was only one man. So why do the people in the ruins think the land surely belongs to them?

answers.text: Because there are many of them

cards.text: That's like saying, "ONE guy got promoted, and there's FIFTY of us in the break room, so obviously we ALL get promoted!" God answers with a list: they eat meat with the blood in it, look to their idols and shed blood.

cards.question: After that list, what does God ask about the people living in the ruins?

answers.text: Whether they should possess the land
Whether they will rebuild the walls

cards.text: And God's list keeps going. They've relied on their swords, committed detestable acts, and each one has defiled his neighbor's wife.

cards.question: After this second list, God asks the people in the ruins once again whether they should possess the land.

cards.text: Then God says, "As surely as I live," and lays it out. The ones in the ruins will fall by the sword, and the ones in the open field He will give to wild animals to be devoured.

cards.question: Those in the ruins fall by the sword, and those in the open field go to wild animals. What about the ones in the strongholds and caves?
God says the mountains of Israel will become so desolate that no one will pass through.

cards.text: The land becomes a desolate waste, and the pride of her strength comes to an end. Ruins, open field, caves... friend, there is NO good spot on that list.

cards.question: God says He will make the land a desolate waste even though the people have done nothing wrong.

cards.text: It's because of all the abominations they've committed. And when it happens, God says, they will know that He is the LORD.
Now God turns to the people right around Ezekiel. They're talking about him near the city walls and in the doorways of their houses.

cards.question: What are the people near the walls and doorways telling each other about Ezekiel?

answers.text: Come and hear the message from the LORD
Stay far away from that prophet
That prophet has lost his mind

cards.text: Ezekiel is the hottest ticket in town, and in all my junk drawer years NOBODY ever told a friend to come hear the stamper! So his people come as usual and sit before him to hear his words.

cards.question: The people who come and sit before Ezekiel put his words into practice.

cards.text: Nope. They express love with their mouths, but their hearts are chasing something else.

cards.question: The people who come to hear Ezekiel express love with their mouths. What are their hearts chasing?

cards.text: Then God gives the picture: to them, Ezekiel is like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument.

cards.question: Why does God say Ezekiel is like a singer of love songs to the people?

answers.text: They enjoy hearing him but don't do it
His messages are all about love
He sings every message he gives

cards.text: It's like your boss gives the whole team a serious warning, everybody claps, says "GREAT meeting!" and changes NOTHING. But God says it will come to pass, and surely it will.

cards.question: When it all comes to pass, God says the people will know that a ___ has been among them.

findings.problem: Abraham shows up in the passage (Ezekiel 33:24) but is never introduced. Card 5 says only 'one man from long ago,' and after card 6 reveals the name, card 7 uses it with no word on who he is. Once card 6 is answered, card 7 could add something like 'Abraham, Israel's forefather' (Genesis 12:1-7) without giving anything away.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 9 already asked about 'Should you then possess the land?' (Ezekiel 33:25). Card 11 asks about the same line again where it repeats in 33:26. The second time the line appears, a story card should tell it, not a choice card.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Card 14 asks about the end of Ezekiel 33:28 (the mountains so desolate no one passes through). No story card has set up verse 28 yet. Card 13 was also a choice card. The start of verse 28 (the desolate waste, the pride of her strength ending) is only told afterward, on card 15. So the baker can only guess at an untold detail, and the passage runs out of order. Card 15's telling of 33:28a should come before this question.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: 'Now God turns to the people right around Ezekiel' reads as if God starts speaking to the people. In Ezekiel 33:30, God is still speaking to Ezekiel ('As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you'). Something like 'Then God tells Ezekiel about his own people' keeps who is being spoken to accurate.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
